overview.title: Church of the Assumption
overview.p1: Portuguese-era church inside the old city — a quiet heritage stop. Adds religious architecture to the military story of Mazagan.
overview.p2: Walk the medina area without rushing; the historic core is compact and pedestrian.
overview.p3: Link this stop with the Portuguese cistern and walls the same half-day.

moods.subtitle: Adds religious architecture to the military story of Mazagan.

1.title: Manueline style
1.desc: Distinct 16th-century European stone features and historic bell tower.

2.title: Look closer
2.desc: Observe the stone masonry and architectural integration into the old medina square.

3.title: Take your time
3.desc: Link this stop with the cistern and ramparts the same half-day.

tips.title: Practical Tips — Church of the Assumption

1.title: Timing
1.desc: Check opening hours or restoration updates the morning of your visit.

2.title: Shoes & pacing
2.desc: Old stone paving inside the medina — wear comfortable walking shoes.

3.title: Combine nearby
3.desc: Link cistern, walls and the church in one half-day heritage loop.

food.title: Eat nearby
food.p1: Cafés and local spots are a short walk away inside the Portuguese city core.
food.p2: Bring water for your medina walk; full meals wait by the seafront.

q1.question: Is there an entry fee?
q1.answer: Exterior views and the surrounding old city square are freely accessible. Interior access depends on restoration work.

q2.question: How long do I need?
q2.answer: 15 to 30 minutes for the church stop; half a day for the full Portuguese core.

q3.question: Best time of day?
q3.answer: Morning or late afternoon for softer light and cooler walking weather in the medina.

q4.question: Combine with what?
q4.answer: Portuguese Cistern, ramparts, and medina souks in one loop.

q5.question: Family-friendly?
q5.answer: Yes for walking ages; enjoy exploring the historic pedestrian lanes safely.
